intro: These are the books shipped with the toolchain on this machine. Everything here opens through this server, so rustdoc search, mdbook search, and every relative link work offline — no internet needed.

items.label: The Rust Programming Language
items.note: The long course. Twenty chapters, three real projects, careful explanations. Start here after finishing this app.

items.label: Rust by Example
items.note: The same ideas told as runnable programs, with exercises at the bottom of each page.

items.label: Standard library API
items.note: Vec, String, HashMap, Iterator, Option, Result — the types you write every day. Has its own search box.

items.label: Core API
items.note: The part of the standard library that works without an operating system.

items.label: Alloc API
items.note: String and Vec without a full standard library.

items.label: The Cargo Book
items.note: Packages, dependencies, workspaces, profiles, publishing to crates.io.

items.label: The rustc Book
items.note: Every compiler flag you will eventually want, including code generation and targets.

items.label: The rustdoc Book
items.note: How to write doc comments and generate the documentation for your own crate.

items.label: The Clippy Book
items.note: The lint collection that reads your code and suggests the idiomatic version.

items.label: Error codes
items.note: The extended explanation behind E0382, E0499, E0502 and every other numbered error.

items.label: Release notes
items.note: What changed in each toolchain release.

items.label: The Rust Reference
items.note: The precise semantics: expressions, patterns, type layout, destructors, attributes.

items.label: The Rustonomicon
items.note: Unsafe Rust, the dark arts: raw pointers, aliasing, unwinding, implementing Vec.

items.label: The Rust Style Guide
items.note: The formatting decisions cargo fmt already made for you.

items.label: The Edition Guide
items.note: What the 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024 editions changed, and how to migrate.

items.label: The Embedded Rust Book
items.note: Bare metal and embedded Linux, for people already comfortable with Rust.

items.label: proc_macro API
items.note: The crate behind derive macros and attribute macros.
